issues.description: The UML in the problem statement marks the Animal(String) constructor as private (shown with '-' in the UML), while the exercise text and the reference solution expect an accessible constructor so subclasses can call super(name). This visibility mismatch could lead students to mistakenly implement a private Animal constructor, which would prevent subclass constructors (Seal, Pig, Goat) from invoking it and thus block correct implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Correct the UML and/or textual description to indicate that Animal(String) must be public or protected (change the UML visibility marker from '-' to '+' or explicitly state visibility). This ensures students know the constructor must be accessible to subclasses (as shown in the reference solution).
